text-faint.purpose: Marks and ornament only. Raised from #545248 (2.74:1 on a raised card); even at #7b7768 it does not clear 4.5:1 on every surface (3.22:1 on surface-3), so informational text belongs in Sepia Dim.

display.purpose: Page titles and the largest single numbers. Neue Haas Grotesk Display Pro.

headline.purpose: Section headings, topic titles, grade letters.

body.purpose: Interface prose — panels, plates, descriptions. The app talking about itself. Futura. NOT the transcript.

caption.purpose: The .fig-caption utility — Epoca Pro Medium Italic. Text that comments on the interface rather than being it: measurement bases, empty states, 'Fig. N —' labels.

label.purpose: The .label-data utility — tabular figures, 0.02em tracking. All chrome controls, chips, and changing numbers. Drops to 10px uppercase / 0.16em in control chrome.

prose.purpose: The transcript reading scale — tutor voice and learner replies. Epoca Pro at 0.9375rem/1.65, larger than interface body because this surface is read continuously for 20–70 minutes rather than scanned.

prose-lede.purpose: Opening paragraph of a reply, 1.06em. Applied only when a second paragraph exists, so a one-line answer is never inflated.

prose-h1.purpose: Top landmark inside a tutor reply. Distinguished by size.

prose-h2.purpose: Section inside a reply. Distinguished by size plus a hairline rule beneath.

prose-h3.purpose: Sub-section inside a reply. Distinguished by uppercase 0.1em tracking rather than size — see The Landmark Rule.

dark.note: Default. Cajal's sepia ink inverted onto the night.

light.note: Re-tunes every token, keeps every meaning. One deliberate split: pure-chrome emphasis (focus ring, frame-hover/selected, dogear, primary button) routes through --color-accent-cta #3d5266 instead of amber. Semantic inks never do.

shadows.name: panel-rest
shadows.purpose: Every .panel. Hairline top catch-light plus a soft high-offset drop.

shadows.name: panel-plate
shadows.purpose: .panel-plate — a full-frame warm inset hairline marking a published answer (the canonical reveal), not one item in a column.

shadows.name: panel-rest-light
shadows.purpose: Light theme. A pale ground needs a warm-ink lift, not a bruise-black drop.

shadows.name: panel-raised-light
shadows.purpose: The light theme's raised panel. A hair brighter on the inset highlight than panel-rest-light (0.6 vs 0.55) — on a pale ground the raised tier has less tonal room to separate, so the top edge does the work the background cannot.

shadows.name: frame-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover/selected frame drawn OUTSIDE the element's own border. Never `outline` — .focus-ring owns that channel. Clipped and invisible on an overflow-hidden host.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Panel border/shadow, row and card hover, view-transition fades.

motion.name: ease-out-soft
motion.purpose: The shared easing for every --dur-base transition.

motion.name: tilt-idle
motion.purpose: Idle drift on card-scale surfaces. Per-card phase so the surface breathes rather than marches.

motion.name: tilt-pointer
motion.purpose: Pointer-follow tilt. The corner under the cursor dips AWAY, as if pressed. Scaled down by SOFT_SCALE / RAIL_SCALE for the quieter tiers.

glass.name: panel
glass.value: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface) 62%, transparent) + backdrop-filter: blur(12px)

glass.name: chat-glass panel
glass.value: 76% — the transcript steps toward opacity so long-form reading sits on steadier ground

glass.name: light theme
glass.value: 78 / 84 / 82 / 90 / 93% — a pale field behind the blur gives a card less to differentiate against

tiltTiers.name: tilt-card
tiltTiers.purpose: Full amplitude. Coach and dashboard surfaces: topic cards, stat blocks, chart-host panels, artifact tiles, history rows.

tiltTiers.name: tilt-card-rail
tiltTiers.purpose: Quieter still. Nav rows and small chrome controls. The multiplier is a CEILING lowered per-axis by a measured edge-throw cap, so a long thin row's sweep across its length is damped while its dip across its depth is untouched. Plates are exempt.

components.name: Glass Panel
components.description: The base surface. Translucent over a 12px blur so the ambient field reads through as weather behind text.

Due today

Eighteen items across four topics.

components.name: Specimen Plate
components.description: The engraved specimen label — a full-frame warm inset hairline instead of a left-edge accent bar, because a canonical reveal is a published answer, not one item in a column.

The Runge–Lenz vector is conserved only for a strict inverse-square force.

STEPS · 3

Expand the potential about the circular orbit.

components.css: .ds-eq-plate { position: relative; display: block; text-align: center; margin: 1.15em 0; padding: 0.95em 2.6em 0.95em 1.15em; border: 1px solid var(--color-hairline); border-radius: 0; background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-surface-2) 45%, transparent); animation: ds-plate-develop 520ms cubic-bezier(0.25,0.8,0.35,1) both; } .ds-eq-body { font-family: 'KaTeX_Main', 'EpocaPro', Georgia, serif; font-size: 1.05rem; color: var(--color-text-primary); } .ds-eq-no { position: absolute; right: 0.9em; bottom: 0.55em; font-family: 'Futura', ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 0.72rem; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--color-text-dim); pointer-events: none; } @keyframes ds-plate-develop { from { opacity: 0; filter: blur(7px); transform: translateY(3px); } to { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0); transform: none; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-eq-plate { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview: Cajal drew the nervous system in sepia ink on paper. This system is that atlas inverted onto the night: a void warmed slightly toward sepia, text in warm paper-ink rather than cold white, and accents in the colors ink takes when it is the only bright thing in a dark room. Every card is a specimen plate, every divider is a dendrite, every figure caption reads 'Fig. N —'. The metaphor is load-bearing. This app is a window onto a spaced-repetition engine, and it exists so a learner sits down for half an hour and retrieves difficult material from memory. An atlas is the right register for that: a record made carefully, over time, of something the maker was trying to understand. So the interface behaves like an instrument panel rather than a product tour — it states what it measured, it does not congratulate, and it holds a dense transcript legibly for the length of a real sitting. The system's own tension is that it is simultaneously very dark, very sharp, and very physical: right angles everywhere, hairline borders, translucent glass over an ambient field, and a card-scale 3D tilt just barely above the threshold of perception. Nothing here is soft. But nothing shouts either — the whole palette lives in a narrow band of luminance, and the loudest thing on screen is usually one amber word.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-black ground (#0d0e12), warm paper text (#e6dfd0) — never a cold gray/white pairing
Zero radius everywhere by decree; rounded-full is the single reserved exception for organic marks
Semantic ink: color encodes memory state, not visual hierarchy
Translucent glass panels (62–82% fill, 12px blur) over an ambient field
Near-subliminal card physics — slow idle drift plus damped pointer-follow tilt
Two motion durations for the entire app: 120ms and 200ms
Density as a feature — a reading surface for thirty-minute sittings

rules.name: The Consolidation Axis Rule
rules.body: Cool and warm are not "accent 1" and "accent 2." Cool means *not yet consolidated*; warm means *survived*. A warm accent on something that has not consolidated is a defect, not a style choice. Nothing may be recolored along this axis for visual balance.

rules.name: The Reserved Danger Rule
rules.body: Danger ink marks a learner's struggle or a lapsed memory. It is never the color of a validation error, a failed network call, a destructive-action button, or a generic alert. Those need their own treatment — usually text, not hue.

rules.name: The Off-Axis Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet marks synthesis and creation. It must never become a third station on the consolidation ramp, and it must never be used simply because a surface needs a third color.

rules.name: The Two Themes, One Semantics Rule
rules.body: The light theme ("Atlas by Daylight", `:root[data-theme='light']`, void `#f4efe4` with `#2b2016` text) re-tunes every token but keeps every meaning. It makes exactly one deliberate split: pure-chrome emphasis — the focus ring, `frame-hover`/`frame-selected`, the dogear, the primary button — routes through `--color-accent-cta` (a grayish blue, `#3d5266`) instead of amber, because on a pale ground amber is emphasis-by-warmth rather than emphasis-by-contrast. Semantic inks (grade colors, threshold violet, danger) never route through that token in either theme.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change in place uses `.label-data`. Tabular figures mean a counter or a timer never makes the layout twitch.

rules.name: The Caption-Is-Commentary Rule
rules.body: Italic serif is not for emphasis inside prose. It marks text that is *about* the interface — a measurement's basis, an empty state, a figure label. If it could be a sentence the tutor said, it is body, not caption.

rules.name: The Landmark Rule
rules.body: A prose heading earns its level by a different *kind* of prominence, never by a slightly larger size. Prose h1 is size, h2 is size plus a hairline rule, h3 is uppercase tracking. This exists because the ramp once ran 1.25 / 1.1 / 1rem above a 0.9375rem body — an h3 at 1.07× the paragraph it introduced — and three heading levels inside a five-pixel range give a long answer no landmarks at all. If a new level is ever needed, give it a new kind of prominence; do not subdivide the sizes.

rules.name: The Paragraph-Gap Rule
rules.body: In prose, the space between paragraphs must exceed the space between lines within one. At `margin: 0.5em` against `line-height: 1.65` it did not, and paragraph breaks — the only structure most tutor replies have — became invisible. Any change to prose leading has to move the paragraph margin with it.

rules.name: The Math-Renders-Everywhere Rule
rules.body: Learner content is graduate-level and routinely contains LaTeX. Any slot that can hold learner or tutor text — including titles, chips, labels and captions, not just prose bodies — passes through the math renderer. A raw `$` on screen is a bug.

rules.name: The Three Tilt Tiers Rule
rules.body: `.tilt-card` (full) is for coach and dashboard surfaces — topic cards, stat blocks, chart hosts, artifact tiles. `.tilt-card-soft` is for every transcript card. `.tilt-card-rail` is for nav rows and small chrome controls by standing decree. These are the same physics at three amplitudes, not three tunings.

rules.name: The Edge-Throw Rule
rules.body: A rotation's felt strength is not its angle but how far it throws the edge it pivots about — `(width / 2) · sin(rotateY)` and `(height / 2) · sin(rotateX)`. Edge throw, not angle, is what the physics tunes: every tier's multiplier is a ceiling, and each axis solves its own angle from the element's measured size so throw stays roughly constant. Below the cap a surface keeps every degree it had, so small elements are untouched and only large ones settle. Transcript cards carry the tightest budget of the three — that surface is being read. Idle drift is held far tighter than pointer tilt, because a card that moves because you moved is feedback while a card that moves on its own as you read is interference. Scrolling stills the surface entirely. A new tilt surface never needs a new tier; the throw budget already covers it.

rules.name: The Chart Doesn't Tilt Rule
rules.body: A chart's SVG never tilts. The panel hosting it does.

rules.name: The Scarce Dogear Rule
rules.body: ACTIVE ONLY, by decree. A dogear on every card in a list is wallpaper; it means something *because* most cards don't have one.

rules.name: The Right Angle Rule
rules.body: Do not reintroduce a radius, at any value, on any surface. If a shape needs softening, it is the wrong shape. `rounded-full` on an organic mark is the only exception.

rules.name: The Unclipped Frame Rule
rules.body: Never apply `.frame-hover` or `.frame-selected` to an `overflow-hidden` host — the inset-negative `::after` gets clipped and silently disappears. Give the frame its own unclipped wrapper, or skip it on that surface.

rules.name: The Formatting Channel Rule
rules.body: MCP bridge cards format prose the tutor would have written anyway — advisory, non-blocking, never load-bearing for the learning loop. A card the loop *depends on* is a design error, not a richer card.

rules.name: The Density Over Ceremony Rule
rules.body: Transcript cards stay compact and scannable. No mark may grow into a full-width panel that breaks the transcript's rhythm; the `92%` cap and tight padding are what make twenty card kinds feel like one surface.

dos: Do encode state in ink: cool for unconsolidated, warm for survived, violet for synthesis, danger for lapse.
Do route every learner- or tutor-authored string through the math renderer, including titles, chips, labels, and captions.
Do use the two motion tokens — `--dur-fast` 120ms for buttons and color shifts, `--dur-base` 200ms with `--ease-out-soft` for panels, rows, cards, and view transitions.

Do reach for `.panel`, `.panel-raised`, `.panel-plate`, `.label-data`, `.fig-caption`, `.focus-ring`, and the `CTRL` recipes before writing new chrome. The idioms exist; a new one is a claim that all of them are wrong.
Do pass `EnvAccent` explicitly on shared components, and keep semantic inks out of it.
Do give a `.frame-hover` or `.frame-selected` element its own unclipped wrapper when the natural host is `overflow-hidden`.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion` — the app-wide kill-switch covers idle drift, pointer tilt, and entry animations, and any new motion must fall under it.
Do keep the transcript dense. It is read for thirty minutes at a stretch.
donts: Don't reintroduce a corner radius anywhere. `rounded-full` on organic marks (dots, rings, pings, the brand glyph) is the only exception.
Don't use danger ink for validation errors, failed requests, or destructive-action buttons. It belongs to the learner's struggle.
Don't promote violet to a third consolidation state, or add a fifth ink because a surface needs another color.
Don't scale anything that isn't a real `<button>` on hover or press — scale is a button-only affordance so it never competes with the border and background cues rows and cards use.
Don't build a bridge card the learning loop depends on. Cards format; they never carry authority.
Don't invent a bespoke focus treatment. `.focus-ring` owns `outline`; the frame vocabulary deliberately uses `::after` so a 2px focus ring always outranks a 1px hover frame.
Don't tilt a chart's SVG. Tilt the panel that hosts it.
Don't treat the open fallback typefaces as an alternate design. They are a degradation path; the licensed mapping is the system.
